ledger.note: 1858: the mainland becomes the Colony of British Columbia. 'The district was converted to a Crown colony on 2 August 1858 by the Parliament of the United Kingdom' (the Fraser gold rush); capital Fort Langley.
1859: New Westminster replaces Fort Langley as capital (infobox 'Fort Langley (1858-1859); New Westminster (1859-1866)').

ledger.note: 1863: the north-east is added. The colony 'was enlarged in 1863 in the north and northeast up to the 60th parallel'; the part not in the Stickeen Territory is read as North-Western Territory land of the Hudson's Bay Company.

ledger.note: 1863: the Stickeen Territories join British Columbia. The territory (19 July 1862 - July 1863; bounded by the 62nd parallel and the 125th meridian) 'was dissolved, most of its former land being added to the Colony of British Columbia'.

region.text: Vancouver Island and the Gulf Islands (the researcher's polygon round the island)

ledger.note: 1866: Vancouver Island is united with British Columbia. 'On 6 August 1866, the united colony was proclaimed, with the capital and assembly in Victoria'; the infobox gives 19 November 1866 for the merger.
1866: Victoria becomes the capital of the united colony ('1866-1871: Victoria', infobox).

region.text: the San Juan Islands, claimed by both Britain and the United States

ledger.note: 1866: the San Juan Islands dispute, begun in 1859 under the Colony of Vancouver Island (twelve-year standoff), passes to the united colony; the start is inherited (confidence 1).

ledger.note: 1871: British Columbia joins Canada. The infobox gives 'Entered Canadian Confederation: 20 July 1871'; British Columbia was admitted 'as the sixth province of Canada on 20 July 1871'.

region.text: British Columbia as the united colony of 1866-1871 and the province of 1871: the mainland, Vancouver Island and the Queen Charlotte Islands

ledger.note: 1871: the Colony of British Columbia ends on 20 July 1871.

certainty.note: No boundary survey on the pages; the 49th parallel is the Oregon Treaty line (sharp), the northern limit approximate.

The 60th parallel and the 120th meridian west are named lines; the boundary with the Alaska panhandle was disputed (Stikine Territory page: until the 1903 Alaska Boundary Settlement). The 49th parallel and the Haro Strait line (after the 1871 arbitration) are the sharp exceptions.

notes: Not a Cliopatria row (Cliopatria draws these years inside British Colonial Empire; the Canada dossier notes British Columbia as drawn there). Pages: Colony of British Columbia (1858-1866) and (1866-1871), Stikine Territory, Colony of Vancouver Island (merger), Pig War (1859) (five). Not on the pages: the 1858 northern boundary, the area, the 51st/55th parallel limits some sources give, the proclamation day at Fort Langley, the Queen Charlotte Islands as a separate colony (the page says the colony 'did include the Colony of the Queen Charlotte Islands'). Disagreements: union 6 August 1866 (proclaimed) vs 19 November 1866 (infobox); Pig War arbitration 1871 on the Pig War page vs 1872 elsewhere; the Stikine Territory page names 125 W as the eastern limit and 62 N as the northern, with the part north of 60 N returned to the North-Western Territory (the Rupert's Land dossier records this). The 1858 'found' has counterpart nobody: the mainland south of the Nass-Finlay line was the Hudson's Bay Company's trading district (the page says only that 'the district was converted to a Crown colony'), which the rupert-s-land dossier does not draw (the Columbia District was a trading right); the northern part, the North-Western Territory, joins in 1863 with rupert-s-land as counterpart.
